title_tag: 美国三年来首次加息！上任不到4个月，川川亲手选的美联储主席就“翻脸”了？—— 早安英文 MORNING ENGLISH 20260920
h1: 美国三年来首次加息！上任不到4个月，川川亲手选的美联储主席就“翻脸”了？
nav_hint: Donald Trump fails to bend the Federal Reserve to his will

headline.en_html: Donald Trump fails to <mark class="voc">bend the Federal Reserve to his will</mark>
headline.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普未能令美联储俯首听命

notes.en: to force someone to do what you want, especially someone who is unwilling
notes.zh: 使某人屈从于自己的意志，让某人听命于自己
notes.ctx: bend 本义“使弯曲”，引申为“使屈服”；标题先给出结论——特朗普想让美联储按他的意思降息，却没能把央行攥进自己手里。
notes.ex1: The new CEO tried to bend the board to his will, but the directors resisted. 新任首席执行官试图让董事会屈从于他的意志，但董事们抵制了。
notes.ex2: No president should be able to bend the central bank to his will. 任何总统都不应能让央行听命于自己。

paragraphs.en_html: Kevin Warsh has <mark class="voc">rebuffed</mark> Donald Trump’s demands for low borrowing costs, as the president’s <mark class="voc">pick</mark> to run the Federal Reserve led it to the first rate rise since 2023 less than four months into the job. The central bank chair on Wednesday offered the strongest evidence yet that he is prepared to <mark class="voc">disregard</mark> Trump when he <mark class="voc">corralled</mark> all 12 rate setters on the Federal Open Market Committee into <mark class="voc">backing</mark> a quarter-point rate rise. “The <mark class="voc">plain</mark> fact is that inflation is too high and has been for too long,” Warsh said, as he repeatedly told journalists that he would be “hard pressed” to describe current interest rates as so high that they would slow the economy.
paragraphs.zh: 凯文·沃什顶住了唐纳德·特朗普要求压低借贷成本的压力——这位总统钦点的美联储掌舵人，上任不到四个月，便推动央行完成了自2023年以来的首次加息。周三，这位美联储主席拿出了迄今为止最有力的证据，表明他准备不理会特朗普：他成功说服联邦公开市场委员会全部12名利率决策者，一致支持加息25个基点。“明摆着的事实是，通胀太高了，而且高得太久了，”沃什说道，并反复向记者表示，他很难将当前的利率水平形容为高到会拖慢经济。

notes.en: to reject someone or something in a blunt or abrupt manner
notes.ctx: 沃什把特朗普压低借贷成本的要求干脆挡了回去，比 refuse 更强调“直接、不给面子”。
notes.ex1: She rebuffed his offer of help with a curt shake of her head. 她干脆地摇了摇头，回绝了他的帮忙。
notes.ex2: The company rebuffed the takeover bid, calling it undervalued. 该公司断然拒绝了收购要约，称其估值过低。

notes.en: a person who has been chosen for a particular role or position
notes.ctx: 这里是名词“钦点的人选”，指特朗普亲自挑中、寄予期待的美联储掌舵人，不是动词“挑选”。
notes.ex1: She was the coach's pick for team captain. 她是教练钦点的队长人选。
notes.ex2: The senator was the president's pick to lead the Treasury. 这位参议员是总统钦点的财政部长人选。

notes.en: to pay no attention to someone or something, especially when you should
notes.ctx: 沃什准备好不理会特朗普——比 ignore 正式，强调“明知该听却不当回事”的故意。
notes.ex1: He disregarded the doctor's advice and kept working late. 他无视医生的建议，继续加班到深夜。
notes.ex2: The committee disregarded the objections of local residents. 委员会对当地居民的反对置之不理。

notes.en: to gather people or things together, especially those who are difficult to control
notes.ctx: 本义“把牲畜赶进围栏”，此处指沃什把 12 名利率决策者全都拢到加息这一边，一个反对票都没落下。
notes.ex1: The manager corralled the whole team into the meeting room. 经理把整个团队都召集到了会议室。
notes.ex2: She managed to corral enough votes to pass the bill. 她设法凑齐了足够的票数让法案通过。

notes.en: to support someone or something, especially with money, votes, or influence
notes.ctx: 12 名决策者一致“力挺”加息 25 个基点；比 support 口语化，常见于政治、金融语境。
notes.ex1: Several major investors backed the startup in its early days. 几家大投资人在早期力挺这家初创公司。
notes.ex2: The union backed the strike by an overwhelming majority. 工会以压倒性多数支持罢工。

notes.en: used to emphasize that something is simple, obvious, and undeniable
notes.ctx: plain fact 是固定搭配，强调事实简单直接、无可辩驳；此处不是“朴素的”，而是“不容否认的”。
notes.ex1: The plain fact is that we cannot afford another delay. 明摆着的事实是，我们经不起再拖了。
notes.ex2: For all the spin, the plain truth is that the project failed. 不管怎么粉饰，明摆着的事实是这个项目失败了。

paragraphs.en_html: Warsh’s signal to Wall Street — just weeks before <mark class="voc">pivotal</mark> midterm elections — that he is ready to take further measures to <mark class="voc">tame</mark> the inflation <mark class="voc">pulsing</mark> across the US economy <mark class="voc">contrasts sharply with</mark> the president’s understanding that he was choosing a Fed boss who “certainly wants to cut rates”.
paragraphs.zh: 沃什向华尔街释放的信号——恰在关键的中期选举前数周——是他准备采取进一步措施，驯服席卷美国经济的通胀。这与总统的认知形成鲜明反差：特朗普以为自己挑选的是一位“当然想降息”的美联储主席。

notes.en: extremely important because it has a decisive effect on the future
notes.ctx: 比 important 更狠，强调“能左右走向”——这场中期选举就是那个转轴。
notes.ex1: She played a pivotal role in the negotiations. 她在谈判中发挥了关键作用。
notes.ex2: This was a pivotal moment in the company's history. 这是公司历史上一个决定性的时刻。

notes.en: to bring something under control, especially something harmful or disorderly
notes.ctx: 本义“驯服野兽”，此处指把通胀这头失控的野兽压下去，常用于通胀、危机语境。
notes.ex1: The government is struggling to tame rising food prices. 政府正努力遏制食品价格上涨。
notes.ex2: It took years to tame the inflation that followed the war. 战后通胀花了数年才被控制住。

notes.en: to move or flow with a strong, regular rhythm; to be full of intense activity
notes.ctx: 脉搏跳动的画面——通胀像心跳一样持续有力地冲击整个美国经济，带动态、蔓延的画面感。
notes.ex1: Excitement pulsed through the crowd as the results came in. 结果揭晓时，兴奋在人群中涌动。
notes.ex2: Anger pulsed through the city after the verdict. 判决之后，愤怒在这座城市里涌动。

notes.en: to be very different from something in a way that is striking or obvious
notes.ctx: 沃什放出的加息信号，撞上特朗普“我选了个想降息的人”的认知；sharply 让这道反差更刺眼。
notes.ex1: Her calm tone contrasted sharply with his angry outburst. 她平静的语气与他的暴怒形成鲜明对比。
notes.ex2: The company's soaring profits contrast sharply with the struggles of its rivals. 该公司飙升的利润与竞争对手的困境形成鲜明对比。

paragraphs.en_html: Trump was quick to hit out at the Fed on Wednesday, saying on his Truth Social platform that “Interest Rates in the United States should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World — BY FAR”. Trump later said he had confidence in Warsh, with whom he has a longstanding personal relationship, and deflected blame on to the Fed board, which includes former chair Jay Powell, whom the president has previously called a “<mark class="voc">moron</mark>” for not lowering rates. It also includes <mark class="voc">governor</mark> Lisa Cook, whom Trump tried to <mark class="voc">sack</mark> before he was stopped by the Supreme Court. “I told Kevin, I said, you might as well vote with the board because it’s just not going to matter. The board is very <mark class="voc">hostile</mark>,” Trump told reporters.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普周三迅速对美联储开火，在其“真相社交”平台上发文称：“美国的利率应该是1%，或者更低，因为我们是全世界最好的信用——遥遥领先。”特朗普随后表示，他对沃什仍有信心，两人私交甚笃；同时他把矛头转向美联储理事会，其中包括前主席杰伊·鲍威尔——总统此前曾因他不降息而骂他是“白痴”。理事会中还有理事莉萨·库克，特朗普曾试图将她解职，但被最高法院拦下。“我跟凯文说了，我说，你干脆跟理事会一起投票算了，反正也没用。理事会敌意很重，”特朗普对记者说。

notes.en: a stupid person (informal, offensive)
notes.ctx: 特朗普骂不降息的鲍威尔用的词，粗鲁带侮辱；新闻直接引用，正是他攻击对手的用词风格。
notes.ex1: He called his opponent a moron during the debate. 他在辩论中称对手是白痴。
notes.ex2: Only a moron would ignore such obvious warnings. 只有白痴才会无视如此明显的警告。

notes.en: a member of the board of a central bank, especially the US Federal Reserve
notes.ctx: 央行语境里不是“州长”，而是美联储理事会成员——莉萨·库克就是这个身份。
notes.ex1: The governor voted against the rate cut. 这位美联储理事投票反对降息。
notes.ex2: She was appointed as a governor of the central bank last year. 她去年被任命为央行理事。

notes.en: to dismiss someone from their job (informal, British)
notes.ctx: 比 dismiss 随意得多，一股“炒掉”的味道——特朗普想炒库克，被最高法院拦住。
notes.ex1: He was sacked for repeatedly missing deadlines. 他因屡次错过截止日期被解雇。
notes.ex2: The manager threatened to sack anyone who leaked the memo. 经理威胁要炒掉任何泄露备忘录的人。

notes.en: unfriendly and opposed to someone or something
notes.ctx: 特朗普说“理事会敌意很重”——不友好、处处作对，带着对抗的火气。
notes.ex1: The proposal met with a hostile reception from shareholders. 该提案遭到股东的敌意对待。
notes.ex2: He faced a hostile audience at the town hall meeting. 他在市政厅会议上面对一群充满敌意的听众。

paragraphs.en_html: Trump’s apparent <mark class="voc">concession</mark> that he is unable to bend the Fed to his will comes as his tariffs and the Middle East conflict have <mark class="voc">conspired</mark> to <mark class="voc">inflame</mark> an affordability crisis that he has <mark class="voc">dismissed</mark> as a “<mark class="voc">hoax</mark>”. “There’s a lot of very clear evidence that the policies of the White House — tariffs and the conflict in the Middle East — have pushed up inflation,” said Claudia Sahm, a former Fed official who is now chief economist at New Century Advisors.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普显然承认自己无法令美联储屈从于他的意志。与此同时，他的关税政策和中东冲突共同加剧了一场“负担能力危机”，而他却将其斥为“骗局”。“有大量非常明确的证据表明，白宫的政策——关税和中东冲突——推高了通胀，”前美联储官员、现新世纪顾问公司首席经济学家克劳迪娅·萨姆表示。

notes.en: a statement or act that admits something is true, often unwillingly
notes.ctx: 不情愿地承认——特朗普等于默认自己动不了美联储，常见搭配 make a concession。
notes.ex1: His silence was seen as a concession that he had been wrong. 他的沉默被视为承认自己错了。
notes.ex2: The government made no concession on the key issue. 政府在关键问题上没有让步。

notes.en: to combine or work together to produce a particular result, often a bad one
notes.zh: 共同导致，凑在一起酿成
notes.ctx: 不是“阴谋”，而是几股力量合力办成一件坏事：关税与中东冲突一起把危机烧得更旺。
notes.ex1: Bad weather and poor planning conspired to ruin the event. 恶劣天气和糟糕的策划共同毁掉了这场活动。
notes.ex2: Several factors conspired to bring about the financial crisis. 多重因素合力酿成了这场金融危机。

notes.en: to make a situation, feeling, or problem worse or more intense
notes.ctx: 本义“使燃烧”，此处是往火里浇油——让危机更烈，常用于矛盾、危机语境。
notes.ex1: His remarks only inflamed the tensions between the two sides. 他的言论只是加剧了双方的紧张关系。
notes.ex2: Rising prices have inflamed public anger. 物价上涨激化了公众的愤怒。

notes.en: to decide that something is not important and not worth considering
notes.zh: 不予理会，斥为，对……不屑一顾
notes.ctx: 不是“解雇”，而是居高临下地打发了事——他把危机一口斥为“骗局”。
notes.ex1: She dismissed the criticism as irrelevant. 她斥之为无关紧要的批评。
notes.ex2: The company dismissed the rumors as pure speculation. 该公司称这些传言纯属猜测，不予理会。

notes.en: a trick or lie intended to deceive people
notes.ctx: 特朗普给“负担能力危机”贴的标签：编出来的假问题，是对手炮制的议题。
notes.ex1: The bomb threat turned out to be a hoax. 炸弹威胁最终被证明是一场骗局。
notes.ex2: He insisted the whole scandal was a hoax. 他坚称整个丑闻是一场骗局。

paragraphs.en_html: Since Warsh’s <mark class="voc">nomination</mark> in January, the big inflation driver has been a rise in petrol and <mark class="voc">diesel</mark> prices — an increase that has cost American <mark class="voc">households</mark> an extra $108bn since the <mark class="voc">outbreak</mark> of the president’s war with Iran, according to a Brown University tracker. “Trump’s tariffs and the war in Iran are driving prices up,” said Jeff Colgan, professor at Brown University. “To a large extent, the inflation that the Fed is fighting is a problem of President Trump’s own making.”
paragraphs.zh: 自沃什1月获得提名以来，通胀的主要推手是汽油和柴油价格上涨。据布朗大学的一项追踪数据，自总统对伊朗开战以来，这一涨幅已让美国家庭多支出1080亿美元。“特朗普的关税和伊朗战争正在推高物价，”布朗大学教授杰夫·科尔根说。“美联储正在对抗的通胀，在很大程度上是特朗普总统自己造成的问题。”

notes.en: the act of officially suggesting someone for a position or job
notes.ctx: 指特朗普 1 月正式提名沃什出任美联储主席那一刻，也是这轮通胀叙事的起点。
notes.ex1: Her nomination to the Supreme Court was confirmed last month. 她对最高法院的提名上月获得确认。
notes.ex2: The nomination process dragged on for weeks. 提名过程拖了数周。

notes.en: a type of heavy fuel used in engines, or a vehicle that uses it
notes.ctx: 与 petrol 汽油并列，是能源涨价里的另一半——柴油一贵，运输物流全跟着贵。
notes.ex1: Diesel prices have risen sharply this year. 今年柴油价格大幅上涨。
notes.ex2: The truck runs on diesel. 这辆卡车烧柴油。

notes.en: all the people living together in one house
notes.ctx: 经济报道的常用计量单位——不是按“人”，是按“一户”来摊这 1080 亿美元。
notes.ex1: The average household spends a quarter of its income on housing. 普通家庭把四分之一的收入花在住房上。
notes.ex2: Rising energy bills are squeezing household budgets. 能源账单上涨正在挤压家庭预算。

notes.en: the sudden start of something unpleasant, especially war or disease
notes.ctx: the outbreak of the war 是固定搭配“战争爆发”——多花的钱就从这一刻开始算。
notes.ex1: The outbreak of war sent oil prices soaring. 战争爆发导致油价飙升。
notes.ex2: Since the outbreak of the pandemic, remote work has become common. 自疫情爆发以来，远程办公已变得普遍。
